_provenance: Geometry, d_max, stdp_lr and batch cloned from exp001_k32-baseline -- the only K=32 configuration with no extra mechanism (exp004 changes d_max, exp005 adds a tie penalty, exp006 adds the drive gene). Rounds raised 136 -> 300 to match every other completed run in the chapter; exp001 stopped at 136 because the engine hung, not by design. Unlike exp001's own config.json, nothing here is reconstructed: this is the configuration as launched.
launch_command: cd experiments/neurodarwinism/exp007_window_first_readout && ND_OUT=$PWD nohup python -u ../src/steady_state.py --pool 32 --rounds 300 --batch 64 --n-val 2000 --stdp-lr 0.01 --d-max 20 --readout-window 48 --coverage-penalty 1.0 --seed-genome <exp002 ck_k128.npz> --ckpt $PWD/ck_window48.npz --tag _window48 > run.log 2>&1 &

under_test._readout_meaning: rank the six outputs on their first spike inside ticks [48, 96), re-based to 0..47; spikes before tick 48 are discarded entirely and an output with none in the window reads 48 (silent)
under_test._penalty_meaning: TRAINING-ONLY. selection fitness = corrected_tau - 1.0 * (mean number of the 6 outputs with no spike in the window, per state). Range of the penalty term is 0..-6, which dwarfs tau's +-1, so coverage dominates until satisfied and ordering takes over afterwards. NEVER applied to the held-out score.

warm_start._why: a random seed genome has almost no output activity, so under a narrow window the whole pool starts at coverage 6/6 and fitness is flat -- selection has nothing to grip. Cloning one evolved genome into all K slots starts the pool somewhere the window can see, and mutation diversifies it from round 1.

held_out_protocol._note: the held-out score is PURE windowed corrected tau. Both the coverage penalty and the tie penalty are training scaffolds and are explicitly passed as 0 in main()'s held-out block and in eval_heldout.py, so the reported number stays comparable with every other experiment. (This is also a behaviour fix: the old held-out call forwarded a.tie_penalty, so an exp005-style run would have reported tau - 0.1*tie_rate as its held-out score.)

why_not_the_original_final_32_design: The first design read the final 32 ticks, [64,96). Measurement killed it before it ran: output spiking on seed genomes stops at tick 33, so that window is empty by construction -- fitness exactly 0.0 for every member, tie rate 1.0, one distinct output vector across 500 states. It was not a seed-genome artefact either: exp002's best evolved genome puts 42 of its 59,971 output spikes at tick >= 64 (windowed fitness +0.0048, 98.6 % silent) and exp004's puts 1,572 of 25,178 (windowed fitness -0.0351). Opening the window at 48 instead of 64, warm-starting from an evolved genome, and adding the coverage penalty are the three changes that give selection something to grip.
missing_control: There is still no matched TTFS baseline on the post-PR#92 engine. exp001 ran 136 rounds pre-fix, so comparing exp007's held-out against its +0.3498 would repeat the cross-engine error documented in the chapter README. A 300-round K=32 TTFS control on the fixed engine is the natural companion run.
